title: Cohomology and quotient maps of a two-term integral coefficient complex
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime, $\Omega$ an algebraically closed field, and $X=\operatorname{Spec}\Omega$. Work on a small skeleton of $X_{\mathrm{proet}}$ in the coefficient universe [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site, def-weil-size-convention]. Let $p_X^*$ be the inverse image from the condensed point [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point], and put $R=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z_\ell}$ and $B_n=p_X^*\underline{\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z}$ for $n\ge1$, with their quotient maps. The underlined rings are the continuous-function condensed rings, and these are the pulled-back coefficient rings [def-weil-l-adic-numbers, sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. Use the canonical finite discrete ring identifications of [lem-pe-condensed-point-discrete-constant-comparisons]. Let $k_X$ be the constant $\mathbf F_\ell$-module sheaf [def-weil-pbc-constant-sheaf], acted on by $B_n$ through reduction modulo $\ell$. Use sheaf modules and sheaf tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product].

Let $P=[R\xrightarrow{\ell}R]$ in cochain degrees $-1,0$, zero elsewhere [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules], and $K=Q_R(P)$ in the unbounded derived category [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Then $P$ is K-flat [def-pc-kflat-complex], its derived reduction $K_n=K\otimes_R^L B_n$ [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings] is represented by $P_n=[B_n\xrightarrow{\ell}B_n]$, and the canonical quotient transition $K_{n+1}\to K_n$ is represented by reduction in both terms. There are $B_n$-linear identifications
$$H^{-1}(K_n)\cong k_X,\qquad H^0(K_n)\cong k_X,\qquad H^q(K_n)=0\quad(q\notin\{-1,0\}).$$
The first identification is the inverse of the map induced, before $p_X^*$, by $\bar a\mapsto\ell^{n-1}a\bmod\ell^n$; the second is induced by reduction modulo $\ell$. Under these identifications the transition on $H^{-1}$ is zero and the transition on $H^0$ is the identity. Moreover $k_X\ne0$, and the canonical action map is an isomorphism
$$H^{-1}(K_{n+1})\otimes_{B_{n+1}}B_n\xrightarrow{\sim}k_X,$$
where the left side uses sheaf tensor and its map to $k_X$ sends $x\otimes b$ to $\bar b x$ after the specified degree-minus-one identification. Thus the map from this tensor product to $H^{-1}(K_n)$ induced by the quotient transition is zero.

proof.text: Tensoring with the free rank-one module is isomorphic to the identity functor, and tensoring with a zero object is a zero functor. Thus both are exact. The double complex has only these flat terms and is bounded above by zero. The independent-universe bounded-flat K-flat theorem makes it K-flat.

source.place: Tag 06YQ, lemma-bounded-flat-K-flat; tensor unit checked directly from sites-modules.tex Tag 03EK

proof.text: The scalar-extension functor sends the regular module to the target regular module by the balanced tensor map b tensor r maps to a(r)b. Additivity identifies the double complexes. The universal derived counit is an isomorphism on the K-flat complex. To compute its actual transition, use the representative and adjunction-normalization equations of Normalization; scalar extension preserves K-flatness and flat terms by the ringed-topos pullback theorem for the identity inverse image. Naturality moves the counits and restriction comparison past the representative. The resulting chain map is the ordinary adjunction unit followed by the scalar-composition map, sending b tensor x to its quotient coefficient tensor x. The preceding regular-module isomorphisms identify it with literal reduction in each nonzero term.

source.place: Tag 06YY, lemma-derived-base-change; Tag 0D6D, lemma-derived-pullback-composition; specified quotient-transition refinement in lem-pe-kflat-scalar-tower-realization

proof.text: Identify the pulled-back discrete residue abelian sheaf with the constant residue sheaf directly. Constant functions give a locally bijective map on the profinite site: the finitely many clopen fibers cover each continuous function, while nonempty test objects detect equality of constants and the empty cover treats the empty object. Sheafification makes this an isomorphism. Pull it back and apply constantSchemeIso. This comparison is used only to identify the residue sheaf and prove its nonvanishing; the kernel and quotient maps themselves retain their specified continuous-postcomposition constructions.

source.place: Clause (2); canonical comparison on finite coefficients and postcomposition maps

proof.text: At Lean index n define the kernel map ZMod(l) to ZMod(l^(n+1)) by multiplication by l^n on integer representatives. The lift is well-defined since l^(n+1) vanishes. Cancellation of the nonzero integer l^n proves injectivity. Integer divisibility identifies its image with the kernel of multiplication by l. Conversely, the kernel of reduction modulo l is the image of multiplication by l. Checking on integer representatives proves linearity for the residue action. These arguments include n=0.

source.place: Final paragraph: explicit elementary coefficient calculation for the non-normalized cohomology witness

proof.text: Build the corresponding internal module maps on continuous functions. Their short complexes are exact sectionwise: choose preimages pointwise, which remain continuous because all finite coefficient rings are discrete. The inverse-image functor on internal modules is exact, and the section-module equivalence is exact. Transport the two short exactness calculations through their composite. The residue comparison with scalar restriction has identity underlying sheaf. Kernel-fork and cokernel-cofork universal properties then supply the two homology isomorphisms of the literal complex, with their specified inclusion and reduction normalizations. Other degrees have zero middle term. The localization homology factorization supplies the derived identifications.

source.place: Tag 093J, lemma-constant-exact; sites.tex Tag 00WJ, lemma-sheafification-exact; module action extension along constant ring sheafification

proof.text: Reduction from the next quotient kills the next kernel inclusion, because l^(n+1) is zero in the current quotient. Reduction followed by the residue map is the next residue map. Naturality of cycles and homology, together with the normalization equations of the two homology isomorphisms, proves that the minus-one map is zero and that the degree-zero map is the identity on the underlying residue sheaf. Composition of restriction of scalars gives the required residue-identity map.

source.place: Final paragraph: maps on cohomology computed using the actual quotient map in both terms

proof.text: For X = Spec of the field, the identity pro-etale object is nonempty. The empty sieve cannot cover it, since a pro-etale covering is jointly surjective. The constant-section map is therefore injective. The distinct elements zero and one of ZMod(l) give distinct constant sections, so the constant residue sheaf, and hence the restricted residue module, is nonzero.

source.place: Tags 00WB, theorem-plus, and 00WK, lemma-sections-sheafification; nonempty pro-etale specialization in the cited node

proof.text: The quotient coefficient map is locally surjective: postcomposition on continuous functions is sectionwise surjective using a discrete continuous choice of lifts, and inverse image preserves its epimorphism. Restriction along a locally surjective ring map is fully faithful, so the scalar-extension/restriction adjunction counit is an isomorphism. Apply this counit to the identified residue module to construct the tensor action isomorphism. The ordinary unit normalization and linearity give its pure-section formula b tensor x maps to b times x. The minus-one cohomology transition is zero by the previous calculation, so its induced balanced map is the zero morphism and has precisely the required pure-section formula.
